results.reason: The check re-renders the committed atlas from data/tour-atlas.json and verifies 160 captured screenshots exist on disk; a sandbox proof would need the full media tree copied per run, so it is exercised by the real gate instead.

The audit currently reports a real backlog of 46 shadowed handlers, so it exits non-zero against the live repo and cannot yet pass the control half of a sandboxed proof. It stays a manual audit until that backlog is cleared, at which point it can move into the gate with a two-sided proof.

The run stage boots the real server on a free port and probes every cron URL, so the check is inherently live. The probe is deliberately unauthenticated and every handler fails closed on CRON_SECRET, so no job body executes: nothing is paid, swapped, minted, transferred, or written. `--static` skips the boot for a route-and-load-only pass.

It reads the production wallet table and the live encryption key, then decrypts in memory to test each secret against the current key. There is no offline fixture for 'this ciphertext no longer opens' that would prove anything about the real fleet. Read-only: it never writes, signs, or broadcasts.

Needs Playwright plus a running server, because the thing under test is how the page behaves when a specific request is aborted or rewritten mid-load. A static fixture cannot fail a fetch the page has not made yet.
